newsitem.title: UK: Crashed KazAir jet probably not insured - brokers.
newsitem.headline: Crashed KazAir jet probably not insured - brokers.

text.p: The hull of the KazAir jet destroyed in a mid-air collision over India on Tuesday was probably not insured, market sources said on Wednesday.

A spokesman for the airline's insurance brokers, Alexander Howden, said: "I am able to confirm that the Russian-built Ilyushin Il-76 aircraft was included on the Kazakhstan National Airways policy for liability only. We are unable to trace a hull insurance policy."
The spokesman said it was very possible that the aircraft hull, likely to be worth less than five million stg ($8 million), was not insured at all.
"It is relatively standard practice for small airlines in such regions to insure for liability only, as they cannot afford hull insurance," the spokesman said.

This means there was insurance for the passengers and crew of the aircraft and possibly for third party damage caused as a result. Howdens believes there were 10 crew members on board and 26 passengers. There may also have been some cargo on board.
The bulk of any liability claims will fall on the London insurance market, but the broker was unable to estimate how much it would cost.
"It will depend on factors such as who was on board and whether anyone was to blame for the accident," he said.
The aircraft was chartered to Kosmokraft, a trading company from neighbouring Kyrgyzstan, transport officials said earlier.
--Gordon Mackenzie Reuters Insurance News +44 171 542 2770 ($ = 0.608 British Pounds Sterling)
